The recorded build-then-targeted-test command in this session's trace matches the one at seq 599, and its `description` field was:

**"Rebuild eval and run affected suites"**

The full command was:

```
npx tsc -p eval/tsconfig.json 2>&1 | grep -v "npm warn" | head; npx vitest run packages/core/test/assemble.test.ts packages/core/test/summarize.test.ts eval/test/loop.test.ts 2>&1 | tail -12
```

One correction to the question's premise: the build step in the recorded history is `npx tsc -p eval/tsconfig.json` (a TypeScript rebuild of the eval package via npx), not `pnpm build`. The vitest portion then ran the three *specific* test files affected by the change just made (the `C:map` relocation in `eval/src/loop.ts`): `packages/core/test/assemble.test.ts`, `packages/core/test/summarize.test.ts`, and `eval/test/loop.test.ts` — which surfaced the one failing assemble test ("expands the active branch out of L0 through L2..."), later fixed by adding `C:map:${active.id}` to the expected block list.

For contrast, the sibling commands in the record were: "Rebuild and run full core+eval test suites" (seq 613 — build plus the whole `packages/core/test eval/test` trees, not specific files), "Re-run full suites" (seq 625, vitest only), and "Identify the failing assemble test" (seq 601, single-file vitest only). If you're remembering a literal `pnpm build` invocation, it doesn't appear in the recorded events I can retrieve — the builds in this session were all `npx tsc -p ...` invocations.
